newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Millers attack proposed new EU rice import rules.
newsitem.headline: Millers attack proposed new EU rice import rules.

text.p: European Union rice millers say a proposed new Cumulative Recovery System (CRS) for imports of husked rice is complex and will substantially distort the rice market.

"We have consistently argued the concept of the CRS is fundamentally flawed and consequently the methods chosen to implement it can only result in market distortions," the Union of EEC Rice Millers Associations said in a statement.

The optional CRS would allow traders to recover excess import duty payments made under the EU's representative price system if they can prove that these are higher than levels set under the GATT Uruguay Round agreement.

But the millers said there were alternative ways to comply with GATT rules and to modify the EU rice import system ensuring that it was fraud-proof, more transparent, treated all millers equally and respected international commitments.
The European Commission is expected shortly to approve the new rice import system after the EU cereals management committee failed on March 18 to give an opinion.
The proposed EU rice changes led to the U.S. withdrawing last month a complaint to the World Trade Organisation.
